title: GOAL Phase E: token diet 2 — no default code review, Jev-gated tool calls, Jev-ranked Planner inputs, worker turn diet, polish backlog
spec: User decision 2026-09-19 14:40: reviews eat tokens without enough return; keep spec review, drop code review except one cheap review for security-touching diffs. Evaluate tool calls with Jev (TypeSafe AI System One model, POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone, typed noul/choice/score answers with probabilities, 0.042 USD per M input tokens, 64k state) the way the LiteLLM guardrail and jev-compactor do: score necessity of each tool call, drop stale tool results, keep everything else verbatim. Also land the polish backlog from the approving Phase C/D reviews. Measured baseline 2026-09-17..19: execute runs average 2.46M cache-read tokens (sonnet, ~1.02 USD), opus reviews 0.73M (1.38 USD), scouts 0.51M; a worker's per-turn baseline context is ~24k tokens (haiku probe: plain 25.8k, --strict-mcp-config 23.8k), so the sink is turn count and accumulated tool results, not tool schemas. Review spend was 45 percent of T-0073 and 44 percent of T-0109. Branch goal/T-0201 from goal/T-0109 (PR 8 base). Order: polish first (c2-3, direct merge), then E1 review policy, then restart the Planner session so the new policy is live, then Jev tasks.
acceptance: Every polish task P1-P8 and E1-E7 merged into goal/T-0201 with a green gate

After E1 merges and the server restarts, a complexity-5 task whose diff touches no security path merges with zero review tasks created; one touching orchestrator/serve.py gets exactly one sonnet review
jev-gate.jsonl shows per-call necessity scores for at least one worker run and the scorecard prints a waste ratio per task
PR goal/T-0201 to main opened for the human
